facts.statement: Saurolophus is a genus of large hadrosaurid dinosaur.
facts.quote: Saurolophus (; meaning "lizard crest") is a genus of large hadrosaurid dinosaur

facts.statement: Saurolophus lived during the Late Cretaceous period in North America and Asia.
facts.quote: Saurolophus (; meaning "lizard crest") is a genus of large hadrosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period of North America and Asia

facts.statement: The type species Saurolophus osborni was described by Barnum Brown in 1912 based on Canadian fossils.
facts.quote: The type species, S. osborni, was described by Barnum Brown in 1912 from Canadian fossils.

facts.statement: The species Saurolophus angustirostris was described by Anatoly Konstantinovich Rozhdestvensky based on specimens from Mongolia.
facts.quote: A second valid species, S. angustirostris, is represented by numerous specimens from Mongolia, and was described by Anatoly Konstantinovich Rozhdestvensky.

facts.statement: Saurolophus is distinguished by a spike-like crest projecting upward and backward from its skull.
facts.quote: Saurolophus is distinguished by a spike-like crest which projects up and back from the skull.

facts.statement: Saurolophus was a herbivore capable of moving on two legs or four legs.
facts.quote: It was a herbivorous dinosaur which could move either bipedally or quadrupedally.

facts.statement: The first remains were found in early Maastrichtian rocks of the Horseshoe Canyon Formation near Tolman Ferry on the Red Deer River in Alberta.
facts.quote: It was found in rocks of early Maastrichtian age, in the Upper Cretaceous Horseshoe Canyon Formation (then known as the Edmonton Formation) near Tolman Ferry on the Red Deer River in Alberta.

facts.statement: A large skeleton of S. angustirostris was recovered by Russian-Mongolian expeditions between 1946 and 1949.
facts.quote: The 1946–1949 Russian-Mongolian paleontological expeditions recovered the large skeleton that became S. angustirostris as described by Anatoly Rozhdestvensky.

facts.statement: Two species are currently considered valid: S. osborni and S. angustirostris.
facts.quote: Two species are regarded as valid today: the type species S. osborni, and S. angustirostris.

facts.statement: S. angustirostris is known from at least 15 specimens.
facts.quote: S. angustirostris (Rozhdestvensky, 1952) is known from at least 15 specimens.

facts.statement: S. angustirostris had a skull 20% longer than S. osborni with snout bones directed more upward.
facts.quote: The Mongolian species had a longer skull (by 20%) and the front of the snout (the premaxillary bones) were more upwardly directed.

facts.statement: S. angustirostris possessed a distinctive row of rectangular scales along its back and tail, known as 'midline feature-scales', which are not preserved in S. osborni.
facts.quote: S. angustirostris also had a distinctive row of rectangular scales along the midline of the back and tail, known as 'midline feature-scales'; these are not currently preserved in S. osborni.

facts.statement: Vertical patterns of scales on the tail flanks of S. angustirostris may have indicated striped coloration in life.
facts.quote: In S. angustirostris, the scales on the tail flank were arranged in vertical patterns, which may have corresponded to striped coloration in life.

facts.statement: S. osborni had radial scale patterns on its tail flanks, possibly indicating mottled or spotted coloration.
facts.quote: This area was covered in radial scale patterns in S. osborni, possibly indicating a more mottled or spotted coloration.

facts.statement: S. osborni was approximately 8.2 to 8.5 meters long with a skull measuring 1.0 meter.
facts.quote: S. osborni, the rarer Albertan species, was around 8.2 - 8.5 m long, with its skull 1.0 m long.

facts.statement: S. osborni is estimated to have weighed around 3 tonnes.
facts.quote: It has been estimated to have weighed around 3 tonne.

facts.statement: S. angustirostris is estimated to have been 12 to 13 meters long and weighed up to 11 tonnes.
facts.quote: The larger Mongolian species S. angustirostris has had its size estimated from 12 m (39 ft) to 13 m long and weighed up to 11 tonne.

facts.statement: Footprints attributed to S. angustirostris suggest it might have grown as large as Shantungosaurus.
facts.quote: However, S. angustirostris might have grown even bigger, as footprints attributed to it suggest sizes similar to Shantungosaurus.

facts.statement: The crest is long and spike-like, projecting upward and backward at about a 45-degree angle from over the eyes.
facts.quote: It is long and spike-like and projects upward and backward at about a 45° angle, starting from over the eyes.

facts.statement: The crest appears solid only at the tip, with internal chambers that may have served respiratory or heat-regulation functions.
facts.quote: This crest is often described as solid, but appears to be solid only at the point, with internal chambers that may have had a respiratory and/or heat-regulation function.

facts.statement: The crest is made almost entirely of nasal bones and is solid in S. angustirostris.
facts.quote: The unique crest of Saurolophus is made up almost completely by the nasal bones, and in S. angustirostris it is solid.

facts.statement: In adult specimens, the crest has a rounded triangular shape in cross-section.
facts.quote: In adult specimens the crests are a rounded triangular shape in cross section.

facts.statement: The premaxilla bones make up nearly 50% of the skull length and are filled with small holes on both sides.
facts.quote: The premaxilla bones make up almost 50% of the entire skull length, and both sides are filled with small holes.

facts.statement: The nasal bones are the longest bones in the skull, extending longer than the premaxilla.
facts.quote: Longer than the premaxilla, the nasal bones are the longest in the skull.

facts.statement: Barnum Brown originally classified Saurolophus in its own subfamily, Saurolophinae, within Trachodontidae.
facts.quote: Barnum Brown, who described the first specimens, put it in its own subfamily in "Trachodontidae" (=Hadrosauridae), the Saurolophinae.

facts.statement: Publications before 2010 typically classified Saurolophus as a member of Hadrosaurinae.
facts.quote: Most publications before 2010 classified Saurolophus as a member of Hadrosaurinae, often known colloquially as the "flat-headed hadrosaurs".

facts.statement: The subfamily Saurolophinae was reinstated in 2010 because Hadrosaurus branched off before the split between hadrosaurines and lambeosaurines.
facts.quote: In 2010, the subfamily Saurolophinae was brought back into use because Hadrosaurus appears to have branched off prior to the "hadrosaurine"–lambeosaurine split.

facts.statement: Saurolophus had a grinding motion analogous to chewing, with teeth packed in batteries containing hundreds of teeth, only a few of which were used at once.
facts.quote: Its skull permitted a grinding motion analogous to chewing, and its teeth were continually replacing and packed into dental batteries that contained hundreds of teeth, only a relative handful of which were in use at any time.

facts.statement: Saurolophus used a broad beak to crop plants and a cheek-like organ to hold food in its jaws.
facts.quote: Plant material would have been cropped by its broad beak, and held in the jaws by a cheek-like organ.

facts.statement: Saurolophus could feed on plants ranging from the ground up to about 4 meters high.
facts.quote: Its feeding range would have extended from the ground to about 4 m above.

facts.statement: James Hopson suggested the crest functioned as a visual signal and proposed that inflatable skin flaps over the nostrils acted as resonators and additional visual signals.
facts.quote: James Hopson supported a function as a visual signal, and further mentioned the possibility that the inflatable skin flaps over the nostrils could have acted as resonators and additional visual signals.

facts.statement: Studies of juveniles indicate that the adult crest was poorly developed in infancy, while the snout grew longer, the orbit became more oval, frontal doming decreased, and the coronoid process grew higher during development.
facts.quote: Based on these juveniles, Dewaele and team indicated that during the ontogeny of S. angustirostris the distinct crest found in adults was poorly developed in infancy, the snout grew proportionally longer, the orbit became more oval-shaped, the doming of the frontal became less prominent, and the coronoid process became higher.

facts.statement: Evidence from the Dragon's Tomb bonebed provides direct proof of social behavior in S. angustirostris, but no such evidence exists for S. osborni.
facts.quote: Bell and team also noted that while Dragon's Tomb provides direct evidence for social behaviour in S. angustirostris, there is yet no evidence for it in S. osborni.

facts.statement: The lack of large wounds on the rest of the skeleton suggests that the Tarbosaurus scavenged an already dead Saurolophus angustirostris.
facts.quote: As suggested by the lack of damage to the rest of the skeleton (such as large wounds in skeletal remains indicative of predation), this tyrannosaurid was likely scavenging an already dead S. angustirostris.

facts.statement: The Saurolophus humerus bears three distinctive feeding marks interpreted as punctures, drag marks, and bite-and-drag marks.
facts.quote: The humerus shows three distinctive feeding methods, interpreted as punctures, drag marks, and bite−and−drag marks.

facts.statement: A 2001 study suggested Saurolophus osborni belonged to a distinct inland fauna associated with Anchiceratops ornatus, distinct from the coastal fauna associated with Pachyrhinosaurus canadensis and Edmontosaurus regalis.
facts.quote: A 2001 study suggested that Saurolophus osborni was part of a distinct inland fauna characterized by an association between Anchiceratops ornatus and it, while the contemporary coastal fauna was characterized by the association of Pachyrhinosaurus canadensis and Edmontosaurus regalis.

facts.statement: The Nemegt Formation environment was semi-arid during certain times of the year.
facts.quote: The area would have been semi-arid during certain times of the year.

facts.statement: Saurolophus angustirostris was common and served as an important large herbivore in the Nemegt Formation.
facts.quote: S. angustirostris was common, and would have been an important large herbivore in the Nemegt Formation.

facts.statement: The genus Saurolophus was established by Brown in 1912.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Brown, 1912

facts.statement: The type species Saurolophus osborni from North America was described by Barnum Brown in 1912.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, Saurolophus osborni, de Norteamérica fue descrita por Barnum Brown en 1912.

facts.statement: The valid species S. angustirostris, which lived in Asia, was described by Anatoly Konstantinovich Rozhdestvensky.
facts.quote: la otra especie válida, S. angustirostris, vivió en Asia, y fue descrita por Anatoly Konstantinovich Rozhdestvensky.

facts.statement: Prieto-Márquez and Wagner described S. morrisi in 2011, but it was reclassified into its own genus, Augustynolophus, in 2014.
facts.quote: Prieto-Márquez & Wagner describieron en 2011 otra nueva especie del género, S. morrisi, pero esta fue reclasificada en su propio género, Augustynolophus, en 2014.

facts.statement: Saurolophus is a genus of two known hadrosaurid ornithopod dinosaur species that lived during the late Cretaceous, approximately 70 to 68 million years ago in the Maastrichtian, in what is now North America and Asia.
facts.quote: Saurolophus ("lagarto crestado") es un género con 2 especies conocidas de dinosaurios ornitópodos hadrosáuridos que vivieron a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 70 y 68 millones de años durante el Maastrichtiense, en lo que es hoy Norteamérica y Asia.

facts.statement: Saurolophus is distinguished by a spike-like crest projecting upward and backward from the skull.
facts.quote: Se distingue por una cresta similar a una púa que se proyectaba hacia arriba y atrás desde el cráneo.

facts.statement: Saurolophus was a significantly large animal that moved on both two and four legs and may have had fewer enemies than other herbivores.
facts.quote: Era un animal significativamente grande que se desplazaba tanto en dos como en cuatro patas y es posible que tuviera menos enemigos que otros herbívoros.

facts.statement: The function of the distinctive spike-like crest of Saurolophus is debated, with multiple interpretations suggesting various roles.
facts.quote: The distinctive spike-like crest of Saurolophus has been interpreted in multiple ways, and could have had multiple functions.

facts.statement: Saurolophus had a duck-billed snout and a small tubular spine-shaped crest on its head.
facts.quote: Saurolophus se caracterizaba por tener un morro en forma de "pico de pato" y una pequeña cresta en forma de espina tubular en su cabeza.

facts.statement: The crest was initially thought to be solid but is hollow inside at the tip, possibly for respiratory or thermoregulatory functions.
facts.quote: La cresta ha sido primero descrita como sólida, pero esto es así sólo en la punta, al parecer posee canales huecos en el interior que podrían tener una función respiratoria o termoreguladora.

facts.statement: The crest is present in both adults and juveniles but is smaller in the younger individuals.
facts.quote: La cresta está presente tanto en adultos como en ejemplares juveniles, pero es más pequeña en estos últimos.

facts.statement: The crest projects upward and backward at a 45-degree angle from between the eyes.
facts.quote: La cresta se proyecta hacia arriba y atrás, saliendo desde entre los ojos a ángulo de 45°.

facts.statement: Saurolophus's unique crest is formed almost entirely by the nasal bones.
facts.quote: La cresta única de Saurolophus está formada casi por completo por los huesos nasales.

facts.statement: In adults, the crests have a rounded triangular cross-section.
facts.quote: En los ejemplares adultos, las crestas tienen una forma triangular redondeada en sección transversal.

facts.statement: Saurolophus could walk on two legs or four legs thanks to its large legs.
facts.quote: Sus grandes patas le permitían caminar de modo bípedo y cuadrúpedo.

facts.statement: S. osborni was estimated to be about 8.2 meters long with a 1-meter skull and a weight of 1.9 tons.
facts.quote: Para S. osborni, la especie de Alberta más rara, se estimo en aproximadamente 8,2 metros de largo, presentando un cráneo de 1 metro y Glut, en 1997, un peso estimado de 1,9 toneladas.

facts.statement: Paul estimated in 2010 that S. osborni weighed around 3 tons.
facts.quote: Paul en 2010 ha estimado que pesaba alrededor de 3 toneladas.

facts.statement: S. angustirostris was larger, measuring about 13 meters long, though larger specimens have been reported.
facts.quote: El S. angustirostris, la especie de Mongolia , era más grande medía aproximadamente 13 metros de largo aunque ejemplares más grandes se han reportado.

facts.statement: S. angustirostris could potentially have weighed up to 11 tons.
facts.quote: Se ha estimado que pesaba potencialmente hasta 11 toneladas.

facts.statement: The largest known S. angustirostris skull measured 1.22 meters in length.
facts.quote: El cráneo más grande conocido de S.angustirostrismide 1,22 metros de largo.

facts.statement: The premaxilla bones make up nearly 50% of the total skull length and are filled with small holes on both sides.
facts.quote: Los huesos de la premaxila constituyen casi el 50% de la longitud total del cráneo y ambos lados están llenos de pequeños agujeros.

facts.statement: Barnum Brown recovered the first Saurolophus remains in 1911, including an almost complete skeleton AMNH 5220.
facts.quote: Barnum Brown recobró los primeros restos de Saurolophus en 1911, incluyendo un esqueleto casi completo, AMNH 5220.

facts.statement: The first remains were found in Maastrichtian sediments of the Horse Canyon Formation (then called Edmonton Formation) near Ferry Tolman on the Red Deer River in Alberta.
facts.quote: Fue encontrado en los sedimentos del Maastrichtiense, en el Cretácico Superior de la Formación Cañón Herradura, conocida en esa época como Formación Edmonton, cerca del Ferry Tolman en el Río Red Deer en Alberta.

facts.statement: Between 1947 and 1949, a Polish-Mongolian expedition recovered a large skeleton described as S. angustirostris by Anatoly Konstantinovich Rozhdestvensky.
facts.quote: Entre 1947 y 1949 la expedición paleontológica Polaco-Mongola recobró el gran esqueleto que sería descrito como S. angustirostris por Anatoly Konstantinovich Rozhdestvensky.

facts.statement: Three partial skeletons were found in the Moreno Formation of California in 1973.
facts.quote: En 1973, tres esqueletos parciales fueron hallados en la formación Moreno de California.

facts.statement: Two species are considered valid: the type species S. osborni and S. angustirostris.
facts.quote: Se conocen dos especies consideradas como válidas, la especie tipo S. osborni, y S. angustirostris.

facts.statement: S. osborni, described by Brown in 1912, is known from a skull and skeleton, two other complete skulls, and cranial fragments.
facts.quote: S. osborni, descrita por Brown en 1912, es conocida a partir de un cráneo y un esqueleto, otros dos cráneos completos y fragmentos craneales.

facts.statement: S. angustirostris, described by Rozhdestvensky in 1952, is known from at least fifteen specimens.
facts.quote: S. angustirostris, descrita por Rozhdestvensky en 1952, es conocido a partir de al menos quince especímenes.

facts.statement: S. kryschtofovici, described by Riabinin in 1930, is not considered valid and is treated as a nomen dubium or synonym of S. angustirostris.
facts.quote: S, kryschtofovici descrito por Riabinin ewn 1930 no es considerada válida, así que se le considera un nomen dubium, o un sinónimo de S. angustirostris, aunque el nombre es anterior a S. angustirostris.

facts.statement: S. angustirostris had a distinctive row of square scales along its back and tail, which was more subtle in S. osborni.
facts.quote: S. angustirostris también tenía una distintiva fila de escamas cuadradas a lo largo de la espalda y cola, la cual era más sutil en S. osborni.

facts.statement: In S. angustirostris, tail scales were arranged in vertical patterns that may have corresponded to striped coloration in life.
facts.quote: En S. angustirostris, las escamas en los lados de la cola estaban dispuestas en patrones verticales, los cuales pueden haber correspondido a una coloración a rayas en vida.

facts.statement: In S. osborni, the tail area was covered with radial scale patterns, likely indicating mottled or spotted coloration.
facts.quote: Por su parte, en S. osborni esta área estaba cubierta con patrones de escamas radiales, lo que probablemente indica una coloración más bien moteada o a manchas.

facts.statement: Until a 2011 re-evaluation by Phil R. Bell, S. angustirostris was not well described.
facts.quote: Hasta una revaluación de la especie realizada en 2011 por Phil R. Bell, S. angustirostris no estaba bien descrita.

facts.statement: Bell found in 2011 that two previous studies of S. angustirostris did not provide a complete enough description to compare the species with S. osborni.
facts.quote: Bell descubrió en una publicación de 2011 que los dos estudios previos de S. angustirostris, realizados por Rozhdestvensky en 1952, y Maryanska y Osmolska en 1981, no proporcionan una descripción lo suficientemente completa para comparar la especie con S. osborni.

facts.statement: Saurolophus lived during the Late Cretaceous Maastrichtian in Alberta.
facts.quote: Fue encontrado en los sedimentos del Maastrichtiense, en el Cretácico Superior de la Formación Cañón Herradura, conocida en esa época como Formación Edmonton, cerca del Ferry Tolman en el Río Red Deer en Alberta.

facts.statement: Saurolophus is considered a hadrosaurine because it possesses a typical hadrosaurine pelvis and a large solid crest.
facts.quote: Saurolophus es considerado como un hadrosaurino, ya que posee una pelvis típica de estos y una gran cresta sólida.

facts.statement: The subfamily name Saurolophinae is the oldest available name for the traditional clade known as hadrosaurines.
facts.quote: Saurolophinae es el nombre más antiguo disponible para el antiguo clado "hadrosaurino".

facts.statement: Saurolophus belongs to the parent group Saurolophini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Saurolophini

facts.statement: Saurolophus is classified in the family Hadrosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Hadrosauridae

facts.statement: Saurolophus belongs to the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Saurolophus lived during the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages, from 83.6 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Like other hadrosaurids, Saurolophus could move bipedally and quadrupedally and was a herbivore that ate a wide variety of plants.
facts.quote: Como todo hadrosáurido, Saurolophus podía moverse en forma bípeda y cuadrúpeda, siendo un herbívoro, comiendo una gran variedad de plantas.

facts.statement: The Saurolophus skull allowed a chewing-like movement, and its teeth were continuously replaced in dental batteries containing hundreds of teeth, though only a handful were used at any given time.
facts.quote: El cráneo permitía un movimiento análogo a la masticación, y sus dientes se substituían continuamente y estaban empaquetados en baterías dentales que contenían centenares de dientes, aunque sólo un puñado de éstos era usado al mismo tiempo.

facts.statement: Saurolophus gathered plant material with a beak and kept it inside its mouth using a cheek-like organ.
facts.quote: El material vegetal era recogido por un pico, y mantenido dentro de la boca por un órgano similar a las mejillas.

facts.statement: Saurolophus fed on vegetation that grew up to four meters tall.
facts.quote: Se alimentaba de la vegetación que se levantaba hasta los cuatro metros de altura.

facts.statement: Saurolophus angustirostris was one of the largest herbivores in the Nemegt Formation.
facts.quote: S. angustirostris es uno de los más grandes herbívoros de la Formación Nemegt

facts.statement: Saurolophus osborni fossils were found in the Horse Canyon Formation alongside other duck-billed dinosaurs such as Edmontosaurus and Hypacrosaurus.
facts.quote: S. osborni fue encontrado en la Formación Cañón Herradura junto a varios otros dinosaurios pico de patos Edmontosaurus y el crestado Hypacrosaurus

facts.statement: The Horse Canyon Formation is interpreted to have had significant marine influence due to the incursion of the Western Interior Seaway.
facts.quote: La Formación Cañón Herradura se interpreta que tuvo una gran influencia marina, debido a la ingresión del Mar interior occidental

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Saurolophus osborni may have preferred to stay on higher ground.
facts.quote: S. osborni puede haber preferido permanecer en tierras más altas.

facts.statement: The Nemegt Formation is interpreted as a zone of abundant humidity, similar to the Dinosaur Park Formation in Alberta.
facts.quote: Nemegt es interpretada como una zona de abundante humedad, como la Formación Dinosaur Park en Alberta.

facts.statement: The distinctive spike-shaped crest of Saurolophus has been interpreted in multiple ways and may have had multiple functions.
facts.quote: La distintiva cresta con forma de púa de Saurolophus se ha interpretado de múltiples maneras, y habría podido tener funciones múltiples.

facts.statement: Barnum Brown suggested that the crest might provide an area for muscle insertion and a connection point for a posterior sail, similar to the Jesus lizard.
facts.quote: Brown lo comparó a la cresta de un camaleón, y sugirió que podría proporcionar un área para inserción muscular y un punto de conexión para una vela posterior como la vista en el lagarto de Jesucristo.

facts.statement: Peter Dodson interpreted similar crest forms in other hadrosaurids as a form of sexual identification.
facts.quote: Peter Dodson interpretó formas similares en otros hadrosáuridos como una forma de identificación sexual.

facts.statement: Maryańska and Osmólska noted a hollow base in the crest, suggesting it expanded the respiratory area to aid in thermoregulation.
facts.quote: Maryańska y Osmólska, notaron una base hueca, sugiriendo que la cresta ampliaba el área respiratoria ayudando a la termorregulación.

facts.statement: James Hopson supported the visual signaling function and mentioned the remote possibility of inflatable skin flaps over the nasal windows acting as resonators and additional visual signals.
facts.quote: James Hopson apoyó la función como señal visual, y mencionó la posibilidad remota de que había aletas inflables de piel sobre las ventanas de la nariz que habrían podido actuar como resonadores y señales visuales adicionales.
